classification.difficultyReason: Construct two separate converse configurations and select suitable AAS/SAS arguments to establish adjacent equal-side pairs, preserving the distinction between a diagonal being bisected and bisecting the other diagonal.

content.prompt: Recall that a kite is a quadrilateral with two pairs of adjacent equal sides. Prove the following properties of a kite. You will need to draw a separate diagram for each point.

children.label: a
children.prompt: If one diagonal of a quadrilateral bisects the two vertex angles through which it passes, then the quadrilateral is a kite.

answer.worked: Let BD bisect angles ABC and ADC. Then $\angle ABD=\angle CBD$ and $\angle ADB=\angle CDB$, while BD is common. Hence $\triangle ABD\cong\triangle CBD$ by AAS. Corresponding sides give $AB=CB$ and $AD=CD$, two pairs of adjacent equal sides, so ABCD is a kite.

spec.description: Kite proof construction with common BD and the two equal angle pairs stated in the proof; no unprovided diagonal bisection assumed.
spec.mathematics: Kite proof construction with common BD and the two equal angle pairs stated in the proof; no unprovided diagonal bisection assumed.

children.label: b
children.prompt: If one diagonal of a quadrilateral is the perpendicular bisector of the other diagonal, then the quadrilateral is a kite.

answer.worked: Let BD be the perpendicular bisector of AC, meeting it at X. Then $AX=CX$, the angles at X are right angles, and BX is common, so $\triangle AXB\cong\triangle CXB$ by SAS. Hence $AB=CB$. Similarly $AX=CX$, DX is common and the included angles are right, so $\triangle AXD\cong\triangle CXD$ by SAS and $AD=CD$. Thus ABCD is a kite. No assumption that $BX=DX$ is made.

spec.description: BD perpendicular bisects AC; AX=CX marks only, B/X/D distances deliberately unequal.
